paper_anchor: Section 3 Part II; Section 4.1 Equations (2)-(3); Table 1; Appendix A.1
exact_statement_under_test: For fifth-order polar Newton-Schulz, PRISM uses g_2(R;alpha)=I+(1/2)R+alpha R^2, chooses alpha in [3/8,29/20] by minimizing the next residual Frobenius norm over the eigenvalues of R=I-X^T X, and does not require an explicit singular-value interval for A.
machine_checks: The implementation contains the exact named residual polynomial.
Every selected alpha is a global minimizer candidate of the quartic loss and is no worse than a 1001-point independent grid to tolerance 1e-8.
At least four distinct alpha trajectories occur across the six distributions and three seeds.
No minimum or maximum singular value is supplied to the PRISM alpha fit.
failure_behavior: The verifier exits nonzero if polynomial-fit optimality or spectrum adaptation checks fail.
scope: Direct full-dimension mechanism verification in singular-value coordinates; dense arithmetic is checked in a separate experiment.
